title: Reference
text:
1 API ownership
BITSZarrDataset is a concrete tensorbids.BITSDataset. The distinction is important when writing a library against BITS:

tensorbids owns backend-neutral dataset operations and protocol types, including queries, record sets, relations, indexing, workspaces, fidelity contracts, and lineage.
bitsio owns the concrete open/create path, Zarr and auxiliary stores, sharded-Parquet engine, image-container ingestion, storage layout, content hashing, and reference resolver.
bitsfuse owns filesystem and MONAI integrations. Its types are not part of the bitsio API.

Depend on the narrowest layer required by your library. Accept a tensorbids.BITSDataset or protocol interface when implementation-specific storage behavior is not required.

title: Copy-on-write workspaces
text:
1 Storage and state
The parent is the dataset or workspace from which a new workspace is opened. The overlay is the storage location that receives new or replaced objects. bitsio stores it under bits/overlays/<id>/. The identifier is derived from the workspace name and the parent’s content state, so the same name opened against the same state produces the same identifier.
The open marker records the workspace name and identifier, its parent, the open time, and two parent-state digests. The content fingerprint covers live tensor content, referenced auxiliary payloads, and relation versions. The history digest covers current lineage-journal heads. A create-once lease serializes commit, discard, and rebase operations.
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
workspace = ds.open_workspace("try")
(marker,) = ds.workspaces().markers
print(workspace.overlay_root.startswith("bits/overlays/exp-"), marker.name, marker.parent)
print(marker.base_fingerprint.startswith("blake3:"), marker.base_history_digest.startswith("blake3:"))
True try (dataset)
True True

title: Copy-on-write workspaces
text:
2 Reads and writes
A workspace view from ds.at(name) searches overlay layers from most specific to least specific. Writes through a writable view go only to its overlay. Nested workspace chains are readable, but bitsio does not yet route writes through more than one overlay, so a nested workspace view is read-only.
While a workspace remains open, direct writes through its parent view raise WorkspaceOpenError. This protects the state recorded in the marker. A commit or discard verifies those digests before changing the parent or removing the overlay.
from tensorbids.exceptions import WorkspaceOpenError

try:
    ds.index()
except WorkspaceOpenError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__, "while", [m.name for m in ds.workspaces().markers], "is open")
WorkspaceOpenError while ['try'] is open

title: Copy-on-write workspaces
text:
3 Commit
A successful commit merges tensors, auxiliary objects, navigators, templates, relations, and producer metadata into the parent. Workspace journal events are appended to the parent journals in order; existing parent events are not rewritten. The executor then rebuilds the parent’s indexes, applies removals and replacements, and removes the overlay.
With the default validate=True, commit verifies that the merged parent has the expected content fingerprint. If the parent’s recorded content or history state has changed, commit returns CommitRefusal without merging. A key changed differently in both parent and overlay also causes a refusal. If the workspace remains valid against the new parent, rebase() updates its pinned state before a retry. See Commit a workspace.

title: Copy-on-write workspaces
text:
4 Discard
Discard removes overlay arrays, relations, and derived indexes. By default it copies the lineage journals and producer metadata to bits/overlays/_discarded/<id>-<attempt>/ and writes the workspace record last. The presence of the record therefore marks a complete archive. It includes the workspace identity, attempt number, lifecycle times, and parent-state digests.
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

exp = ds.at("try", read_only=False)
exp.write_array("sub-01/ses-test/anat/sub-01_ses-test_desc-try_mask.nii", np.ones((4, 4, 4), "uint8"))
outcome = exp.discard()
print(outcome.mode, outcome.archive_root.startswith("bits/overlays/_discarded/exp-"), outcome.archive_root.endswith("-1"))
print(sorted(p.name for p in (Path("ds000114.bits") / outcome.archive_root).iterdir()))
ds.open_workspace("try")
table = ds.at("try").lineage_table()
print(table.filter(table["source_tree"] == "overlay").height)
physical True True
['_record.json', 'provenance']
0
Archiving outside the active overlay allows the same workspace name and identifier to be opened again without inheriting discarded data. Each discard increments the attempt number. purge() permanently removes one archived attempt, while discard(purge=True) skips archival.
If the underlying byte store cannot delete objects, the executor performs a logical discard: it removes the active marker but must leave the overlay bytes and record in place. The identifier cannot be reused until those objects are purged through a deletion-capable store.

title: Copy-on-write workspaces
text:
5 Concurrency model
Workspace terminology resembles version-control terminology, but the behavior is intentionally narrower. Commit does not perform a three-way content merge; it requires the parent state to match or returns a refusal. Rebase updates the recorded parent state but does not resolve conflicting array values. A discarded archive retains lineage and workspace metadata, not the deleted array content, so it cannot be checked out as a historical dataset state.

title: Persistent BIDS index and query semantics
text:
1 The index
The BIDS index has one row per navigator that materializes a BIDS-visible file. Internal navigators that only produce stored tensors do not appear. Each row includes the target path, content hash, standard path components, BIDS entities, fidelity contract, output specification, referenced store keys, and schema-defined metadata columns.
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
table = ds.query(suffix="bold").table
print(table.height, "rows,", table.width, "columns")
print(table.select("subject", "session", "task", "contract_level", "RepetitionTime").head(2))
4 rows, 71 columns
shape: (2, 5)

│ str     ┆ str     ┆ str            ┆ str            ┆ f64            │

Read sidecar fields through ds.sidecar(ref); do not use these index columns for filtering until metadata population is implemented.
bitsio stores the BIDS index as subject-partitioned Parquet under bits/bids-index/. BITSDataset.index() rebuilds the BIDS and provenance indexes. auto_create() and a successful workspace commit invoke it, but individual write methods do not:

The provenance index has the same freshness requirement. If it already exists, lineage() and lineage_table() read the persisted snapshot; a newly written key is absent until the next index() call. See Export data lineage as W3C PROV.

title: Persistent BIDS index and query semantics
text:
2 Entities and filters
Filters accept a BIDS entity’s long or short name as defined by the BIDS schema. A scalar requires equality; a list, tuple, or set accepts any member. Query.REQUIRED selects rows where the entity is present, while Query.OPTIONAL imposes no presence requirement.
from tensorbids.query import Query

print(len(ds.query(acquisition=Query.REQUIRED)), len(ds.query(task="fingerfootlips")), len(ds.query(task=["fingerfootlips"])))
print(len(ds.query(ses="retest")) == len(ds.query(session="retest")))
print(len(ds.query(modality="func")), len(ds.query(datatype="func")))
0 4 4
True
4 4
For pybids compatibility, modality is an alias for the datatype directory. It does not refer to the BIDS mod entity.

title: Persistent BIDS index and query semantics
text:
3 Sidecar inheritance
BIDS metadata inheritance applies matching sidecars from general to specific locations in the source tree. During ingestion, the BIDS source adapter resolves that chain for each image. A more specific value replaces an inherited value as a whole, including nested objects. The merged JSON document is stored as a content-addressed auxiliary payload referenced by the navigator’s sidecar_ref parameter.
Consequently, normal reads do not traverse a sidecar hierarchy. Changing the source dataset after ingestion has no effect on the BITS dataset; use set_sidecar() to replace stored metadata. The current validation layer checks whether a sidecar is present for suffixes that require one, but it does not validate every required field inside that sidecar.

title: Persistent BIDS index and query semantics
text:
4 Relations
Relations have declared keys, also called their grain. Participants and splits are keyed by subject; phenotype relations may add session; run-level relations such as events use the entities that identify their run. records() assembles model records from relations and image references, query_relation() filters one relation, and join() joins the BIDS index with relations. See Import tabular data.

title: Persistent BIDS index and query semantics
text:
5 Compared with pybids
pybids constructs a BIDSLayout index from a BIDS tree and resolves metadata according to the indexed file hierarchy (Yarkoni et al. 2019). A BITS dataset stores the index and resolved sidecars as part of the dataset. Opening is therefore independent of a source-tree scan, but writes become queryable only after an index rebuild. tensorbids provides a limited BIDSLayout compatibility interface over the stored index for get, get_file, get_subjects, get_metadata, and related calls.

title: Architecture and library responsibilities
text:
1 Motivation
A conventional BIDS dataset (Gorgolewski et al. 2016) represents an image as a file, commonly a gzip-compressed NIfTI, and derives metadata by applying BIDS sidecar inheritance to the file’s path. This representation is well suited to exchange and command-line tools. It is less efficient when an application repeatedly reads small spatial regions: gzip decompression begins at the start of the stream, and sidecar inheritance must be resolved before metadata can be used.
BITS retains the BIDS-visible paths and file semantics while allowing the underlying numerical values, metadata, and relations to use storage optimized for their access patterns. Chunked arrays support region reads; merged sidecars avoid repeated inheritance resolution; and a persistent relational index serves BIDS entity queries.

title: Architecture and library responsibilities
text:
2 Processing model
The main objects have distinct roles:

A source adapter scans an external dataset and produces a typed manifest.
The dataset writer stores numerical arrays, auxiliary payloads, and relations. It also writes a navigator for each virtual file. A navigator is a typed operation graph that references stored data and describes how to reconstruct the file.
The index records BIDS entities and other query fields for each navigator.
A query returns navigator references. The resolver evaluates each selected navigator as reconstructed bytes, an image object, or a numerical array.
Record sets join image references with relation columns and can translate lazy spatial selections into tensor-store region reads.

This separation allows array chunking, compression, sharding, and backend selection to change without changing the BIDS target path or reconstruction logic.

title: Architecture and library responsibilities
text:
3 Library boundaries







Library
Responsibility




tensorbids
BITS models and protocols, including navigators, storage and resolver interfaces, queries, record sets, workspaces, and provenance operations


bitsio
Zarr v3 tensor storage, content-addressed auxiliary storage, a sharded-Parquet table engine, container ingestion, and the NumPy-based reference resolver


bitsfuse
User-facing integrations over a BITS dataset, including filesystem projection, writable staging, and MONAI adapters



Libraries that consume BITS should depend on tensorbids for protocol types when they do not require a specific backend. Depend on bitsio when the concrete storage implementation or reference resolver is required. Code that uses the MONAI adapters should depend on bitsfuse.

title: Architecture and library responsibilities
text:
4 Fidelity and provenance
The resolver does not infer data quality from a file extension. Each navigator has a mechanically derived fidelity contract:

lossless: reconstructed bytes are preserved;
semantically_lossless: interpreted values are preserved although the byte representation may differ;
mask_lossless: values are preserved within a declared spatial support; and
lossy: reconstruction introduces a declared loss, such as affine quantization.

Provenance is represented separately. The navigator explains how stored data becomes a virtual file; the append-only lineage journal records how each stored array was created, changed, or removed. This distinction lets clients inspect file fidelity and data origin independently.

title: Architecture and library responsibilities
text:
5 Conformance requirements
The BITS specification names three dataset guardrails:







Requirement
Practical implication for bitsio




G1: bounded requests and read amplification for training samples
Chunk and shard geometry must be selected for the application’s read regions. Chunk-aligned reads perform best; arbitrary windows trade request count against excess decoded data.


G2: sufficient data to reconstruct supported BIDS files
Navigators retain the arrays and auxiliary payloads required for reconstruction. NIfTI content is reconstructed, but source gzip framing is not retained.


G3: complete provenance and a trusted manifest state
Lineage journals and producer metadata are stored with the dataset, and freezing records content and history digests.



These are conformance targets rather than performance guarantees for every layout. In particular, no single chunk geometry is optimal for both whole-file reads and arbitrary small windows. See Storage backends and array layout.

title: Architecture and library responsibilities
text:
6 Relationship to established tools
NiBabel (Markiewicz et al. 2026) implements neuroimaging file formats and image objects. pybids (Yarkoni et al. 2019) indexes and queries BIDS file trees. MONAI (Cardoso et al. 2022) provides medical-imaging transforms and data pipelines. BITS does not replace these concerns: bitsio provides an alternative physical representation and resolver, while bitsfuse provides adapters to file- and MONAI-oriented workflows.

from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
table = ds.lineage_table()
print(table.height, "keys;", table.columns[:6])

14 keys; ['subject', 'store_key', 'target_path', 'content_hash', 'lineage', 'realization']
shape: (1, 4)

The table contains one row per current stored array, including its subject, target path, content hash, origin, storage status, producer, source record, last event, fidelity contract, layout, and storage layer. It is a Polars data frame, so ordinary expressions can select lossy rows or workspace rows (source_tree == "overlay").
Call ds.index() after writes. If a provenance index exists, lineage_table() reads that persisted snapshot and does not include later writes until the next index build.

title: Export data lineage as W3C PROV
section: 2 Record what a write was made from
text:
2 Record what a write was made from
Pass an IngestSource when a write was derived from another dataset object:
import numpy as np
from tensorbids.provenance.ingest_record import IngestSource

(source,) = ds.query(subject="01", suffix="T1w")
(t1w,) = ds.read(target_path=source.target_path, form="tensor")


class Volume:
    def __init__(self, data, affine):
        self.data, self.affine, self.shape = data, affine, data.shape


(image,) = ds.read(target_path=source.target_path, form="object")
target = "sub-01/ses-test/anat/sub-01_ses-test_desc-brain_T1w.nii"
volume = Volume((t1w * (t1w > t1w.mean())).astype("float32"), image.affine)
ds.write_volume(
    volume,
    target_path=target,
    geometry=ds.default_geometry(volume, target),
    ingest_record=IngestSource(source_ref=source.target_path),
)
ds.index()
(row,) = ds.lineage_table().filter(ds.lineage_table()["target_path"] == target).to_dicts()
key = row["store_key"]
print(row["lineage"], row["ingest_record"])
root {"source_ref":"sub-01/ses-test/anat/sub-01_ses-test_T1w.nii","consent":null}

Committing a workspace merges its overlay into its parent and closes the workspace. The parent may be the base dataset or another workspace, although the current bitsio implementation supports writes only in workspaces opened directly from the base dataset.

title: Commit a workspace
text:
1 Commit
import numpy as np
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
ds.open_workspace("mask")
exp = ds.at("mask", read_only=False)
key = exp.write_array("sub-01/ses-test/anat/sub-01_ses-test_desc-brain_mask.nii", np.ones((4, 4, 4), "uint8"))
outcome = exp.commit()
print(type(outcome).__name__, outcome.overlay_id.startswith("exp-"))
print(outcome.scopes_appended, outcome.keys_removed, outcome.unfrozen)
print(ds.lineage(key).source_tree, ds.workspaces().markers)
CommitOutcome True
('01',) () False
base ()
exp.commit() closes the workspace addressed by exp. ds.commit(workspace="mask") performs the same operation from the base dataset. A successful commit rebuilds the parent’s indexes and returns a CommitOutcome describing the merged journal scopes and store keys. The keys_removed, keys_retained, and keys_relocated fields report how the storage implementation handled replaced data.

title: Commit a workspace
text:
2 Handle a concurrent parent change
Each workspace records the state of its parent when it opens. If two sibling workspaces start from the same state, the first commit changes the parent. A subsequent commit returns CommitRefusal rather than merging against an unexpected parent state:
ds.open_workspace("a")
ds.open_workspace("b")
ds.at("a", read_only=False).write_array("sub-02/ses-test/anat/sub-02_ses-test_desc-a_mask.nii", np.ones((4, 4, 4), "uint8"))
ds.at("b", read_only=False).write_array("sub-03/ses-test/anat/sub-03_ses-test_desc-b_mask.nii", np.ones((4, 4, 4), "uint8"))
ds.commit(workspace="a")
refused = ds.commit(workspace="b")
print(type(refused).__name__)
print(refused.reason.split(" (")[0])
CommitRefusal
base fingerprint drifted since the experiment opened
If the workspace’s changes remain valid against the updated parent, rebase it and retry the commit:
rebased = ds.rebase(workspace="b")
print(rebased.marker_repinned)
print(type(ds.commit(workspace="b")).__name__)
True
CommitOutcome
A conflicting store key can also cause a refusal; store_key identifies the conflict. With the default validate=True, the implementation verifies that the merged parent has the expected fingerprint and raises WorkspaceLifecycleError if validation fails.

title: Commit a workspace
text:
3 Nested workspaces
The protocol permits a workspace to have another workspace as its parent. bitsio can read such nested overlays, but it does not yet route writes through multiple overlay layers. A nested workspace therefore opens read-only:
from tensorbids.exceptions import TensorBIDSError

ds.open_workspace("outer")
ds.at("outer", read_only=False).open_workspace("inner")
try:
    ds.at("inner", read_only=False)
except TensorBIDSError as error:
    print(str(error).split(";")[0])
print(sorted(marker.name for marker in ds.workspaces().markers))
workspace 'inner' is nested
['inner', 'outer']
For writable work, open the workspace directly from the base dataset. An outer workspace cannot commit while a child workspace remains open.

title: Commit a workspace
text:
4 Commit through bitsfuse
bitsfuse commit ds000114.bits --workspace mask
The bitsfuse command is the CLI integration for writable mounts. It prints the resulting fingerprint on success or the refusal reason on failure, and it does not commit while staged files remain pending.

title: Commit a workspace
text:
5 Constraints

While a workspace is open, direct writes to its parent raise WorkspaceOpenError.
A concurrent commit, discard, or rebase can acquire the workspace lease. Another lifecycle operation then raises WorkspaceLeaseError until the lease is released.
Rebase does not merge conflicting content. Inspect a refusal before deciding whether retrying against the new parent is valid.

└─────────┴───────┴──────┘
Values with significant leading zeros, such as 001, remain strings. To set a type explicitly, supply Dtype in the data dictionary or construct an in-memory frame with the required schema.

title: Import tabular data
text:
3 From a data frame
A Polars or pandas data frame, or an Arrow table, retains its column types. The writer records those types as Dtype entries in the stored data dictionary:
import polars as pl

frame = pl.DataFrame({"subject": ["01", "02", "03"], "score": [101.5, None, 97.0], "site": ["001", "002", "001"]})
print(ds.write_table("phenotype/scores", frame).write.dtypes)
{'subject': 'string', 'score': 'float64', 'site': 'string'}
Writing the same registered relation again replaces its contents and increments its version. When called through a workspace view, the write is isolated in that workspace.

title: Import tabular data
text:
4 Describe the columns
Use dictionary to provide BIDS data-dictionary entries. Supplied fields override inferred metadata for the named columns:
ds.write_table(
    "phenotype/scores",
    "scores.csv",
    dictionary={
        "score": {"Description": "Task score", "Units": "points"},
        "site": {"Description": "Scanner site"},
    },
)
print(ds.phenotype("scores").columns)
['subject', 'score', 'site']
The dictionary is stored as the relation sidecar and is emitted as JSON by export_bids(). Declare categorical levels explicitly; they are not inferred.

text:
5 Use the tables
As fields of a record set:
from tensorbids.query import BIDSReference

records = ds.records(BIDSReference(suffix="T1w"), "phenotype/scores.score", "split/folds.fold")
print(len(records), records.table.columns)
print(len(records.where(fold=0)))
3 ['subject', 'T1w', 'phenotype/scores.score', 'split/folds.fold']
2
With missing="drop" (the default), the record set retains only subjects that have every requested component. A bare column name is accepted by where() when it is unambiguous. Use query_relation() to query a relation without joining it to images.

export_bids() does not export split relations.
The table write path does not currently enforce the dataset’s read-only setting. Open the dataset with read_only=False before writing and do not rely on the current permissive behavior.

title: Inspect lineage and export provenance
text:
1 Read the lineage
Every stored-array write appends an event to a lineage journal. The lineage table presents the current state obtained by folding those events, with one row per stored array:
table = exp.lineage_table()
(row,) = table.filter(table["target_path"] == target).to_dicts()

print(lineage.lossy, lineage.contract_level)
print([entry.kind.value for entry in exp.history(key).entries])
root stored True lossy overlay
True lossy
['ingest']
The row reports a stored, lossy array written to an overlay. lineage() returns the typed report for one store key, while history() returns all journal entries associated with that key.






NoteBIDS provenance comparison



BIDS GeneratedBy records dataset-level provenance. BITS additionally tracks events for individual stored arrays. The two mechanisms are complementary.

title: Build records and batches

WarningContent review status

Join one image per subject with fields from tabular relations, apply a lazy spatial crop, and iterate over batches suitable for a model.

title: Build records and batches
text:
1 Add a table
Create a relation that assigns each subject to one of two folds. Reopen the dataset in writable mode before adding the relation:
import polars as pl

from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
subjects = ds.subjects()
folds = pl.DataFrame({
    "subject": subjects,
    "fold": [n % 2 for n in range(len(subjects))],
})
written = ds.write_table("split/folds", folds)  # idempotent
print(written.name, written.write.dtypes)
split/folds {'subject': 'string', 'fold': 'int64'}
The registered name "split/folds" identifies this relation as a subject split named folds. write_table() accepts an in-memory data frame or a path to a CSV or TSV file. For an in-memory frame, the writer preserves the declared column types.

title: Build records and batches
text:
2 Build a record set
A BITS record set joins image references and relation columns at a shared key. The following record set contains one T1-weighted image, the participant’s dominant hand, and the assigned fold for each subject:
from tensorbids.query import BIDSReference

records = ds.records(
    BIDSReference(suffix="T1w"),
    "participants.dominant_hand",
    "split/folds.fold",
)
print(records)
columns = ("subject", "participants.dominant_hand", "split/folds.fold")
print(records.table.select(columns).head(4))
print(len(records.where(fold=0)))
BITSRecordSet(10 records, key=['subject'], references=['T1w'], fields=['participants.dominant_hand', 'split/folds.fold'])
shape: (4, 3)
┌─────────┬────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│ subject ┆ participants.dominant_hand ┆ split/folds.fold │
│ ---     ┆ ---                        ┆ ---              │
│ str     ┆ str                        ┆ i64              │
╞═════════╪════════════════════════════╪══════════════════╡
│ 01      ┆ left                       ┆ 0                │
│ 02      ┆ right                      ┆ 1                │
│ 03      ┆ right                      ┆ 0                │
│ 04      ┆ right                      ┆ 1                │
└─────────┴────────────────────────────┴──────────────────┘
5
BIDSReference selects image rows from the BIDS index. A string of the form "relation.column" selects a relation column. The join key is inferred from the selected data; this example produces one record per subject. Records with a missing component are dropped by default. Pass missing="error" to reject incomplete joins. where(fold=0) filters the assembled records.

title: Build records and batches
text:
3 Batching data for models
The T1-weighted images do not all have the same shape, so they cannot be stacked directly. A record function requests a 64 x 64 x 64 window from each image and renames the output fields. The window remains lazy until the loader resolves the batch, allowing the backend to read only the required array region.


crops.py

def crop(record):
    """A random 64-voxel cube of the T1w image, and the label."""
    return {
        "T1w": record["T1w"].random_window(i=64, j=64, k=64),
        "hand": record["participants.dominant_hand"],
    }







WarningData loader workers



With the recommended forkserver or spawn process start method, each worker imports the record function by module and name. Define the function in an importable module, rather than as a notebook-local function or lambda.


import torch

from crops import crop

loader = records.select(crop, seed=0).loader(batch_size=2, shuffle=True, stack=True)
data = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
    loader,
    batch_size=None,
    num_workers=2,
    persistent_workers=True,
    multiprocessing_context="forkserver",
)
for epoch in range(2):
    loader.set_epoch(epoch)
    batch = next(iter(data))
    t1w = batch["T1w"]
    print(epoch, type(t1w).__name__, tuple(t1w.shape), t1w.dtype, batch["hand"])
0 Tensor (2, 64, 64, 64) torch.float32 ['left', 'left']
1 Tensor (2, 64, 64, 64) torch.float32 ['right', 'left']
records.loader() already produces complete batches, so the outer PyTorch DataLoader uses batch_size=None. set_epoch() changes the deterministic shuffle order and random-window draws for the next epoch in every worker.






WarningWorkers and the main module



In a script, protect the training entry point with if __name__ == "__main__": so that worker imports do not run the training loop.








NoteBITS and MONAI



The record-set loader is a tensorbids data-loading interface. The temporary MONAI integration is maintained by bitsfuse; see Use BITS data in a MONAI pipeline.

from tensorbids.query import Query

text:
WarningContent review status



This page contains unreviewed content created with large language model (LLM) tools.
This chapter creates a copy-on-write workspace over the dataset from part one and writes a quantized copy of one BOLD image to that workspace. The base dataset remains unchanged. The following chapters inspect the write’s lineage, export it as W3C PROV, and discard the workspace while retaining an audit record.

title: Use a copy-on-write workspace
text:
1 Before you start
Open the ds000114.bits dataset created in part one with workspace operations enabled:
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
print(len(ds.query(suffix="bold")), "BOLD runs")
4 BOLD runs

title: Use a copy-on-write workspace
text:
2 Open a workspace
A workspace is an isolated overlay over a dataset or another workspace. Open one named "int8-bold", then obtain a writable view of that overlay:
from tensorbids.exceptions import WorkspaceOpenError

WORKSPACE_NAME = "int8-bold"
ds.open_workspace(WORKSPACE_NAME)
exp = ds.at(WORKSPACE_NAME, read_only=False)
print([marker.name for marker in ds.workspaces().markers])
try:
    ds.write_table("split/other", ds.split("folds"))
except WorkspaceOpenError as error:
    print("refused:", type(error).__name__)
['int8-bold']
refused: WorkspaceOpenError
ds continues to address the base dataset, while exp reads the workspace overlay before falling back to the base. While a workspace is open, writes to its parent are rejected with WorkspaceOpenError. This restriction allows a later commit or discard to verify that the parent has not changed since the workspace was opened.






NoteWorkspace identity



The workspace identifier is derived from its name and the recorded state of its parent. A workspace ends by committing its changes or discarding them.

title: Use a copy-on-write workspace
section: 3 Write a run as int8 codes
text:
3 Write a run as int8 codes
Read subject 01’s BOLD run and write a quantized version whose stored codes span the full int8 range:
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from tensorbids.authoring import AffineQuantization
from tensorbids.provenance.ingest_record import IngestSource


@dataclass
class Volume:
    """Values to write, with their affine; a 4-D run is time first."""

    data: np.ndarray
    affine: np.ndarray

    @property
    def shape(self):
        return self.data.shape


(source,) = exp.query(subject="01", session="test", suffix="bold")
(image,) = exp.read(target_path=source.target_path, form="object")
bold = np.moveaxis(image.get_fdata(dtype="float32"), -1, 0)
volume = Volume(bold, image.affine)
rung = AffineQuantization.spanning(bold.min(), bold.max(), "int8")
target = "sub-01/ses-test/func/sub-01_ses-test_task-fingerfootlips_desc-int8_bold.nii"
exp.write_volume(
    volume,
    target_path=target,
    geometry=exp.default_geometry(volume, target, dtype="int8"),
    precision=rung,
    ingest_record=IngestSource(source_ref=source.target_path),
)
exp.index()
print(f"scale {rung.scale:.4f}, offset {rung.offset:.4f}")
(written,) = exp.read(target_path=target, form="tensor")
print("largest error", float(np.abs(written - bold).max()), "<=", rung.scale / 2)
(nifti,) = exp.read(target_path=target, form="object")
print(nifti.shape == image.shape, np.allclose(nifti.affine, image.affine))
scale 16.7647, offset 2145.8824
largest error 8.35302734375 <= 8.382352941176471
True True
AffineQuantization.spanning() derives a linear scale and offset from the observed value range. Quantization introduces an error of at most half a scale step, so the navigator’s fidelity contract is lossy. IngestSource records the source BOLD path in the lineage of the new stored array.






WarningA 4-D volume is written time first



write_volume() expects a four-dimensional volume in (time, i, j, k) order and restores NIfTI’s time-last order when materializing the file. Move the time axis explicitly before writing, as shown above; the API cannot infer an incorrectly ordered input array.








NoteNIfTI scaling comparison



The BITS tensor store contains the int8 codes directly. The reconstructed NIfTI object exposes dequantized float32 values; it is not an int8 NIfTI using scl_slope and scl_inter. The record-set API can return the codes and their scale parameters separately.

title: Use a copy-on-write workspace
text:
4 Train on the codes
Select the stored port and attach the scale and offset instead of dequantizing during the read:
import torch
from tensorbids.query import BIDSReference

codes = exp.records(
    BIDSReference(suffix="bold", desc="int8", port="stored", dequantize="attach")
)
data = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(codes.loader(batch_size=1, stack=True), batch_size=None)
batch = next(iter(data))
q = batch["bold"]
print(q.dtype, tuple(q.shape))
print(batch["bold.scale"].tolist() == [rung.scale], batch["bold.offset"].tolist() == [rung.offset])
values = q.double() * batch["bold.scale"].view(-1, 1, 1, 1, 1) + batch["bold.offset"].view(-1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
print(np.allclose(values[0].numpy(), written, rtol=1e-5))
torch.int8 (1, 184, 64, 64, 30)
True True
True
The batch contains int8 codes plus one scale and offset per record. Apply the affine transformation on the target device or inside the model. The result matches the resolver’s dequantized float32 read to numerical precision.
Lazy spatial windows work with stored codes in the same way as in part one:


windows.py

def window(record):
    """A random 32 x 32 x 16 crop of every frame of the run's codes."""
    return {"bold": record["bold"].random_window(i=32, j=32, k=16)}

from windows import window

crops = codes.select(window, seed=0).loader(batch_size=1, stack=True)
batch = next(iter(torch.utils.data.DataLoader(crops, batch_size=None)))
print(batch["bold"].dtype, tuple(batch["bold"].shape), batch["bold.scale"].tolist() == [rung.scale])
torch.int8 (1, 184, 32, 32, 16) True
A window retains the scale and offset of its source image because the affine dequantization is independent for each value.






WarningA workspace’s records stay in process



Record sets backed by a workspace view cannot currently be serialized to PyTorch worker processes. Use the default num_workers=0 for these loaders.








NoteMONAI distinction



Quantization is part of the stored representation, not a MONAI transform. The loader returns the stored codes and their scaling parameters.

Finish the workspace example in the same Python session. Discard the workspace, inspect the retained audit record, and then delete that record permanently.

title: Discard the workspace
text:
1 Discard the changes
exp.commit() would merge the workspace into its parent. This example discards the changes instead:
exp.discard()
print(ds.lineage(key))
print([(record.name, record.attempt) for record in ds.discarded_workspaces()])
old = ds.discarded("int8-bold")
print([entry.kind.value for entry in old.history(key).entries], old.lineage(key).lossy)
print(len(old.lineage_table()), "rows")
None
[('int8-bold', 1)]
['ingest'] True
15 rows
Discard removes the overlay’s arrays and tables, so the base dataset remains unchanged. It archives the workspace record, journal, and producer metadata; lineage remains available even though the int8 array cannot be read. Reopening int8-bold creates a clean workspace. Each later discard creates a new numbered attempt, selectable with ds.discarded("int8-bold", attempt=n). Call purge() to delete one archived attempt permanently:
removed = old.purge()
print(len(removed) > 0, ds.discarded_workspaces())
True []






WarningA store that cannot delete



If the underlying store does not support deletion, discard can only remove the workspace logically. Its bytes and metadata remain at the overlay location, and the workspace name cannot be reused until a deletion-capable store purges the retained data.

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
WarningContent review status

A layout profile selects a chunk shape, shard shape, and compression codec for each stored array according to its data type and axis labels. tensorbids defines the profile and registry interfaces; bitsio provides four profiles for its Zarr backends.

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
1 List the registered profiles
from tensorbids.resolver.layout_profiles import layout_profiles

for name, profile in sorted(layout_profiles().items()):
    print(name, [rule.name for rule in profile.rules], "base:", profile.base)
bitsio.archival ['int16-3d'] base: bitsio.unsharded
bitsio.default ['int16-3d', 'float32-3d', 'int8-3d', 'int16-time', 'int16-direction', 'other'] base: None
bitsio.fast ['int16-3d', 'float32-3d', 'int8-3d', 'int16-time', 'int16-direction'] base: bitsio.default
bitsio.unsharded ['int16-3d', 'float32-3d', 'int8-3d', 'int16-time', 'int16-direction', 'other'] base: None








Profile
Picks
Use it for




bitsio.default
Approximately 64-voxel chunks with Zstandard-based compression; usually one shard per array
General-purpose reads with a low object count


bitsio.unsharded
Default chunking with one object per chunk
Storage systems that handle many small objects efficiently


bitsio.archival
Whole-volume int16 chunks compressed with zstd@19; otherwise inherits bitsio.unsharded
Infrequently read data where compression ratio is the priority


bitsio.fast
Lower compression levels with sharding
Ingestion and write throughput

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
2 Create a dataset with one
ds, report = BITSZarrDataset.auto_create(source, "dest.bits", profile="bitsio.archival")
write_source() accepts the same profile argument.

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
3 Preview a layout before writing
from tensorbids.resolver.layout_profiles import resolve_layout

t1w = resolve_layout((256, 156, 256), "float32", ("i", "j", "k"), "bitsio.default")
print(t1w.rule, t1w.chunk_shape, t1w.codec, t1w.shard_shape((256, 156, 256), t1w.chunk_shape))
bold = resolve_layout((184, 64, 64, 30), "int16", ("time", "i", "j", "k"), "bitsio.archival")
print(bold.profile, bold.rule, bold.chunk_shape, bold.codec)
float32-3d (64, 64, 64) blosc-zstd@9:byteshuffle (256, 192, 256)
bitsio.unsharded int16-time (16, 32, 32, 30) blosc-zstd@9:byteshuffle
If no rule matches, resolution continues with the profile’s base profile. bitsio.archival defines a rule for three-dimensional int16 arrays. The four-dimensional BOLD array therefore falls back to bitsio.unsharded.

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
4 Fork a profile
from tensorbids.resolver.layout_profiles import LayoutRule

lab = layout_profiles()["bitsio.default"].fork(
    "lab.bold-frames",
    LayoutRule(
        "int16-time",
        "zstd@9",
        dtypes=frozenset({"int16"}),
        axis_labels=("time", "i", "j", "k"),
        grid=(1, 64, 64, 30),
    ),
)
frames = resolve_layout((184, 64, 64, 30), "int16", ("time", "i", "j", "k"), lab)
print(frames.profile, frames.rule, frames.chunk_shape, frames.codec)
lab.bold-frames int16-time (1, 64, 64, 30) zstd@9
fork() copies the original rules and base profile. A rule with an existing name replaces that rule; a newly named rule is evaluated before the copied rules.

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
5 Register it
In a process:
from tensorbids.resolver.layout_profiles import register_layout_profile

register_layout_profile(lab)
register_layout_profile(lab)
print("lab.bold-frames" in layout_profiles())
True
Registering an equivalent profile a second time is idempotent. Registering a different profile under the same name raises ValueError. Libraries should publish profiles through the tensorbids.layout_profiles entry-point group:
[project.entry-points."tensorbids.layout_profiles"]
"lab.bold-frames" = "lab.layouts:BOLD_FRAMES"

title: Configure array chunking and compression
text:
6 Override one write
chunk_shape= and codec= on auto_create or write_source take precedence over the profile for every array of that call:
ds, report = BITSZarrDataset.auto_create(source, "dest.bits", codec="zstd@19")

text:
7 Constraints

Rules match data types and axis-label sequences, not BIDS suffixes. For example, a T1-weighted image and a three-dimensional mask with the same data type match the same rule.
Explicit chunk_shape and codec arguments override the profile but are applied to every image in that ingestion call.

title: Control stored numerical precision
text:
WarningContent review status

Use exact narrowing during ingestion when the source values admit a smaller representation. Use explicit affine quantization when a bounded numerical error is acceptable and should be represented in the file’s fidelity contract.

title: Control stored numerical precision
text:
1 Narrow exactly at ingest
auto_create and write_source take narrowing=:








narrowing=
Looks at
Stores




"header" (default)
the header only
the source dtype, with the header’s scaling as stored


"range"
every value
the smallest integer dtype that holds them, if all are finite whole numbers


"step"
every value
int codes on a uniform step (at most 65,536 distinct values), if they rebuild every value bit for bit; else as "range"



All three modes preserve numerical values exactly. If the requested analysis cannot find a smaller exact representation, ingestion retains the original representation.
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset
from bitsio.example_data import fetch_ds000114

for narrowing in ("header", "range", "step"):
    _, report = BITSZarrDataset.auto_create(fetch_ds000114(), f"{narrowing}.bits", narrowing=narrowing)
    print(narrowing, [(s.suffix, s.dtype) for s in report.strata])
header [('T1w', 'float32'), ('bold', 'int16')]
range [('T1w', 'float32'), ('bold', 'int16')]
step [('T1w', 'float32'), ('bold', 'int16')]
This dataset does not narrow further: its T1-weighted values are continuous floating-point data, and its BOLD values are already int16. Label maps, masks, and integer-valued data stored in a floating-point container are more likely to benefit.

title: Control stored numerical precision
text:
2 Quantize values to int8
import numpy as np
from tensorbids.authoring import AffineQuantization


class Volume:
    def __init__(self, data, affine):
        self.data, self.affine, self.shape = data, affine, data.shape


ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
(image,) = ds.read(subject="01", suffix="T1w", form="object")
t1w = image.get_fdata(dtype="float32")
volume = Volume(t1w, image.affine)
rung = AffineQuantization.spanning(t1w.min(), t1w.max(), "int8")
target = "sub-01/ses-test/anat/sub-01_ses-test_desc-int8_T1w.nii"
ds.write_volume(
    volume,
    target_path=target,
    geometry=ds.default_geometry(volume, target, dtype="int8"),
    precision=rung,
)
ds.index()
(values,) = ds.read(target_path=target, form="tensor")
print(values.dtype, float(np.abs(values - t1w).max()) <= rung.scale / 2)
(row,) = ds.query(target_path=target).table.select("contract_level").to_dicts()
key = ds.lineage_table().filter(ds.lineage_table()["target_path"] == target)["store_key"][0]
print(row["contract_level"], ds.lineage(key).lossy)
float32 True
lossy True
AffineQuantization.spanning(low, high, dtype) maps the minimum and maximum integer codes to low and high. Values are rounded to the nearest code, so the maximum quantization error is half of one scale step. For a four-dimensional volume, pass values in (time, i, j, k) order.

title: Control stored numerical precision
text:
3 Read values or codes
Normal reads return dequantized values. To retrieve the stored codes together with their scale and offset, select the stored port and attach the dequantization parameters:
from tensorbids.query import BIDSReference

codes = ds.records(BIDSReference(suffix="T1w", desc="int8", port="stored", dequantize="attach"))
(c,) = codes.read([0])["T1w"]
print(c.q.dtype, c.q.shape, c.dtype, np.allclose(c.q * c.scale + c.offset, values, rtol=1e-5))
int8 (256, 156, 256) float32 True
In records(...).loader(), a Codes value is collated into three fields: T1w for the int8 codes, T1w.scale, and T1w.offset. Lazy windows retain the scale and offset of their source image.

A reconstructed NIfTI contains dequantized float32 values, not int8 values encoded with scl_slope and scl_inter.
write_array() stores the supplied data type without creating an image fidelity contract. Do not cast to a lossy data type before calling it. Use a container writer such as write_volume() with an explicit precision rung.

from bitsfuse.monai import BitsDataset
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset
from tensorbids.query import BIDSReference, BIDSReferenceType

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits")
records = ds.records(
    BIDSReference(suffix="T1w", return_type=BIDSReferenceType.METATENSOR),
    "participants.dominant_hand",
)
dataset = BitsDataset(records)
item = dataset[0]
image = item["T1w"]

10 ['T1w', 'participants.dominant_hand', 'subject']
MetaTensor (256, 156, 256) torch.float32 (4, 4)
Each item retains the record fields. A METATENSOR reference becomes a MetaTensor in NIfTI axis order, with affine and spatial_shape metadata; a TENSOR reference becomes a torch.Tensor. The default output data type is float32. Pass float16, bfloat16, float64, or native to select a different type. The optional transform argument applies a MONAI dictionary transform to each item.

title: Use BITS data in a MONAI pipeline
text:
2 Inside an existing pipeline
Use LoadBITSImaged where an existing dictionary pipeline would otherwise use LoadImaged. The transform resolves BIDS target paths through the open dataset:
from bitsfuse.monai import LoadBITSImaged

load = LoadBITSImaged(["image"], dataset=ds, ensure_channel_first=True)
(ref,) = ds.query(subject="02", suffix="T1w")
loaded = load({"image": ref.target_path, "label": 1})
print(type(loaded["image"]).__name__, tuple(loaded["image"].shape), loaded["label"])
MetaTensor (1, 156, 256, 256) 1
A missing target path raises RecordError. With allow_missing_keys=True, the transform leaves absent keys unchanged.

3 Batch
Images with different shapes cannot be stacked directly. Crop or pad them to a common shape with a MONAI transform or a BITS record function before batching:
from monai.transforms import CenterSpatialCropd, EnsureChannelFirstd, Compose
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

crop = Compose([EnsureChannelFirstd("T1w", channel_dim="no_channel"), CenterSpatialCropd("T1w", (64, 64, 64))])
loader = DataLoader(BitsDataset(records, transform=crop), batch_size=2)
batch = next(iter(loader))
print(tuple(batch["T1w"].shape), batch["participants.dominant_hand"])
(2, 1, 64, 64, 64) ['left', 'right']

records.loader() can translate a lazy spatial window into region reads of the stored arrays. BitsDataset reads each selected image before applying its MONAI transform. Use the record-set loader when partial array reads are the priority, and use BitsDataset when reusing an existing MONAI transform pipeline is more important.

For spawn or forkserver workers, transforms and record functions must be importable by module and name.

[('threshold', 2)]

On a store without deletion support, discard is logical: bytes and metadata remain at the workspace root, and its name cannot be reused until a deletion-capable store purges them.
The archive supports provenance inspection, not reconstruction of deleted array values.

title: Storage backends and array layout
text:
1 Implemented storage components
A tensor store maps an opaque key to an n-dimensional array. bitsio provides Zarr v3 implementations backed by TensorStore or zarr-python. Both backends read arrays written by the other when they support the selected codec. Storage roots may use a local directory, memory, S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure; the supported combinations depend on the selected backend and transport.
An auxiliary store maps a content hash to a smaller payload such as an affine matrix, image header, or resolved JSON sidecar. Equal canonical payloads share one key. Array-valued payloads use a fixed little-endian .npy representation for each payload kind; floating-point zero and NaN values are canonicalized before hashing. The store can use hash-partitioned objects or packfiles.
A table engine stores BIDS relations, user-defined relations, and the BIDS and provenance indexes as sharded Parquet.
A navigator is a typed operation graph defined by tensorbids. It references tensor and auxiliary keys and describes reconstruction steps such as reading, exact casting, affine dequantization, spatial selection, and file materialization. bitsio stores navigators through the tensorbids dataset filesystem and evaluates them with its reference resolver.

title: Storage backends and array layout
text:
2 Tensor content hashes
A tensor content hash covers its data type string, including byte order, its shape, and its C-order values. It does not cover chunk boundaries, compressed bytes, or backend metadata:
import numpy as np
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset, canonical_tensor_hash

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
values = np.arange(4 * 5 * 6, dtype="float32").reshape(4, 5, 6)
a = ds.write_array("sub-01/anat/sub-01_desc-a_T1w.nii", values, codec="zstd@19")
b = ds.write_array("sub-01/anat/sub-01_desc-b_T1w.nii", values, chunk_shape=(2, 5, 6), codec="blosc-zstd@5:byteshuffle")
print(ds.tensor.info(a).codec, "|", ds.tensor.info(b).codec, ds.tensor.info(b).chunks)
print(ds.tensor_hash(a) == ds.tensor_hash(b) == canonical_tensor_hash(values))
print(canonical_tensor_hash(values.astype(">f4")) == canonical_tensor_hash(values))
zstd@19 | blosc-zstd@5:byteshuffle (2, 5, 6)
True
False
The first result shows that the same values have the same hash under different codecs and chunk shapes. The second shows that byte order is part of tensor identity. A storage-only change can therefore be recorded as a relayout event without claiming that the tensor values changed. Store keys are opaque; applications should not parse their current textual representation.

title: Storage backends and array layout
text:
3 Layout
An array plan fixes an array’s shape, data type, chunk shape, shard shape, and codec. A layout profile is an ordered set of rules that matches data types and axis-label sequences. The first matching rule supplies the physical layout. If no local rule matches, selection continues in the base profile.








Profile
Base
Rules




bitsio.default
none
Approximately 64-voxel chunks; Zstandard-based compression; generally one shard per array


bitsio.unsharded
none
Default chunk geometry with one object per chunk


bitsio.archival
bitsio.unsharded
Whole-volume int16 chunks compressed with zstd@19


bitsio.fast
bitsio.default
Lower compression levels with sharding



A rule does not inspect BIDS suffixes. Arrays with the same data type and axis labels therefore select the same rule even when their BIDS meanings differ. See Configure array chunking and compression for profile customization.

title: Storage backends and array layout
text:
4 Read amplification
Read amplification is the ratio between data read or decoded and data requested by the application. The G1 conformance target combines low amplification with a small number of range requests. For a window of side \(W\), placed uniformly along an axis of length \(n\) and chunked with extent \(C\), the number of chunks touched is
\[
k(o) = \left\lfloor \frac{o + W - 1}{C} \right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \frac{o}{C} \right\rfloor + 1,
\qquad o \in \{0, \dots, n - W\},
\]
For cubic chunks and windows, the expected decoded amplification is \(\prod_{\text{axes}} \mathbb{E}[k] \cdot C^3 / W^3\). The following calculation uses a \(64^3\) window in a (256, 156, 256) float32 image:
import numpy as np

W, shape = 64, (256, 156, 256)


def chunks_touched(n, C):
    o = np.arange(n - W + 1)
    return (o + W - 1) // C - o // C + 1


print("chunk  chunks/window  decoded/needed")
for C in (16, 32, 64, 128):
    k = np.prod([chunks_touched(n, C).mean() for n in shape])
    print(f"{C:>5}  {k:>13.2f}  {k * C**3 / W**3:>13.2f}x")
chunk  chunks/window  decoded/needed
   16         120.09           1.88x
   32          26.07           3.26x
   64           7.75           7.75x
  128           2.29          18.31x
The default profile stores these images in \(64^3\) chunks within one shard. The next cell reads the shard indexes for the nine tutorial images with this shape and estimates compressed bytes fetched for random windows:
import json
from pathlib import Path

fetched, stored = [], []
for meta in sorted(Path("ds000114.bits/bits/tensors/arrays").glob("*/zarr.json")):
    m = json.loads(meta.read_text())
    if m["data_type"] != "float32" or tuple(m["shape"]) != shape:
        continue
    (shard,) = [p for p in meta.parent.glob("c/**/*") if p.is_file()]
    grid = tuple(s // 64 for s in m["chunk_grid"]["configuration"]["chunk_shape"])
    raw = shard.read_bytes()
    table = np.frombuffer(raw[-(np.prod(grid) * 16 + 4) : -4], "<u8").reshape(*grid, 2)
    nbytes = np.where(table[..., 0] == 2**64 - 1, 0, table[..., 1]).astype(float)
    stored.append(nbytes.sum())
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)  # the same windows in every shard
    for _ in range(1000):
        origin = [rng.integers(0, n - W + 1) for n in shape]
        fetched.append(nbytes[tuple(slice(o // 64, (o + W - 1) // 64 + 1) for o in origin)].sum())
print(len(stored), "shards;", f"{np.mean(fetched) / 2**20:.2f} MiB fetched per window of", f"{np.mean(stored) / 2**20:.1f} MiB stored")
print(f"a window's decoded values: {W**3 * 4 / 2**20:.0f} MiB; the whole volume: {np.prod(shape) * 4 / 2**20:.1f} MiB")
9 shards; 1.37 MiB fetched per window of 5.8 MiB stored
a window's decoded values: 1 MiB; the whole volume: 39.0 MiB
The example illustrates three design considerations:

Smaller chunks reduce excess decoding for arbitrary windows but increase the number of touched chunks and storage objects or ranges.
Chunk-aligned samples avoid boundary overlap and provide the most predictable I/O cost.
Sharding reduces object count and can co-locate chunk ranges, but the reader must first obtain the shard index. Readers cache that index after the first access.

Compression changes the byte-level result: the measured random window fetches only part of the compressed shard, whereas a gzip-compressed NIfTI generally requires decompression from the start of the stream.

title: Storage backends and array layout
text:
5 Precision
A writer can reduce stored precision in two distinct ways:

Exact narrowing during ingestion analyzes the header, value range, or a uniform exact step. It changes storage only when reconstructed values remain exact, so the navigator’s fidelity contract does not weaken.
Affine quantization maps values to integer codes with a declared scale and offset. It introduces bounded error and produces a lossy contract.

write_array() stores the supplied array directly and does not author an image fidelity contract. See Control stored numerical precision.

title: Storage backends and array layout
text:
6 Compared with a NIfTI file
A .nii.gz file is a single gzip stream, so a reader normally decompresses from the start of that stream. A chunked BITS tensor can read and decode only the chunks intersecting the requested region. Its content hash covers tensor type, shape, and values rather than compressed storage bytes.

title: Record assembly and batched loading
text:
1 Definitions
A BIDSReference selects one image for each record and defines the requested representation:

the return type is TENSOR, METATENSOR, OBJECT, or BYTES;
the port selects the reconstructed image tensor or a named navigator port, including "stored"; and
dequantize="attach" returns integer codes with their scale and offset as a Codes value instead of applying the scale during the read.

A relation field is addressed as <relation>.<column>. A bare column name is accepted when it is unambiguous among the selected relations.
The record key determines the unit of observation. By default, tensorbids derives it from the BIDS entities that vary among the selected references and includes subject when present. The optional key argument overrides that choice. Each assembled record must contain one value for every reference and field; missing="drop" removes incomplete records, while missing="error" rejects them.
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset
from tensorbids.query import BIDSReference

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits")
print(ds.records(BIDSReference(suffix="T1w")).key)
print(ds.records(BIDSReference(suffix="bold")).key)
print(len(ds.records(BIDSReference(suffix="T1w"), BIDSReference(suffix="bold"))))
('subject',)
('subject', 'session')
2
The T1-weighted selection varies by subject, whereas the BOLD selection varies by subject and session. Their combined key is therefore (subject, session). Only subject/session pairs that contain both image types remain.

title: Record assembly and batched loading
text:
2 Lazy reads
Inside a record function, tensor references are represented by LazyTensor objects. Basic indexing, random_window(), and bound_to_mask() update a read plan without loading data. When a batch is evaluated, compatible operations are reduced to rectangular array regions and submitted together. The tensor store reads the chunks intersecting those regions; see read amplification.
Random-window sampling derives its generator state from the record-set seed, epoch, record index, and reference name. A fixed seed and epoch therefore produce the same windows across worker processes. seed=None requests non-deterministic draws.
def crop(record):
    return record["T1w"].random_window(i=32, j=32, k=32)


windows = ds.records(BIDSReference(suffix="T1w")).select(crop, seed=0)
first, again = windows.read([0]), windows.read([0])
windows.set_epoch(1)
print((first[0] == again[0]).all(), (first[0] == windows.read([0])[0]).all())
True False
With stack=True, values for each reference are stacked along a batch axis. All arrays must have a common shape; fixed-size windows satisfy this condition even when their source images differ. OBJECT and BYTES results are not stacked.

title: Record assembly and batched loading
text:
3 The loader
loader() returns a PyTorch IterableDataset whose items are already complete batches. Wrap it with torch.utils.data.DataLoader(batch_size=None) to avoid a second batching layer. Workers partition the epoch’s batch order. in_flight limits outstanding reads, while slots controls reusable shared-memory buffers. set_epoch() updates both shuffle order and deterministic random windows.
With the recommended forkserver or spawn process start method, a worker starts a fresh interpreter and imports the record function by module and name. Define the function in an importable module and protect executable script code with if __name__ == "__main__":. Record sets backed by workspace views are not currently serializable to worker processes and must use num_workers=0.

title: Record assembly and batched loading
text:
4 Compared with MONAI
The record-set interface is defined in tensorbids and can exploit bitsio region reads before data reaches the application. MONAI (Cardoso et al. 2022) provides a broader transform ecosystem around item dictionaries and MetaTensor. bitsfuse.monai.BitsDataset adapts BITS records to that interface, generally reading the selected image before applying MONAI transforms. See Use BITS data in a MONAI pipeline.

title: Data lineage and provenance
text:
1 Definitions
A navigator is a typed operation graph from stored keys to a virtual file. Its fidelity contract is inferred from the graph: byte-preserving lossless, value-preserving semantically_lossless, spatially bounded mask_lossless, or lossy.
A journal event records one operation affecting a store key. Journals are partitioned by subject. The event types are:







Event
Records




ingest
A key receives stored data from an external source or a producer recipe


relayout
The same tensor values move to another physical layout


remove
A key is removed from the current dataset state


condense
A computed result is materialized in storage


evert
Stored data is retired in favor of recomputation from a producer recipe


rebase
A producer recipe is updated to reference a new source state


derive
A derived relation column is recorded



Each event includes the preceding journal hash. Changing an earlier entry therefore invalidates all later hashes in that journal. Workspace commit appends the workspace entries to the parent’s journal; commit itself is not a lineage event.
A producer recipe is a navigator whose output is a derived store key. The provenance index folds journal events into the current state of each key. lineage(key) reads that state, while history(key) selects the journal entries associated with the key.
import polars as pl
from bitsio import BITSZarrDataset

ds = BITSZarrDataset.open("ds000114.bits", read_only=False)
table = ds.lineage_table()
(row,) = table.filter((pl.col("subject") == "01") & pl.col("target_path").str.contains("T1w")).to_dicts()
key = row["store_key"]
lineage = ds.lineage(key)
print(lineage.lineage.value, lineage.realization.value, lineage.from_index, lineage.lossy)
print([entry.kind.value for entry in ds.history(key).entries])
print(lineage.ingest_record.source_ref)
root stored True False
['ingest']
sub-01/ses-test/anat/sub-01_ses-test_T1w.nii.gz
When a provenance index exists, lineage reads use the last persisted snapshot. Call index() after writing; otherwise a new key may be absent from lineage() and lineage_table().

title: Data lineage and provenance
text:
2 Contracts and loss
When a container write authors a lossy navigator, for example through affine quantization to int8, the ingest event records that contract and the key’s lineage reports lossy. write_array() writes a tensor without authoring a virtual image or image fidelity contract. See Control stored numerical precision.

title: Data lineage and provenance
text:
3 The PROV mapping
ds.prov() maps the current lineage of selected keys to the W3C PROV data model (PROV-DM):







PROV
From




prov:Entity
A store key and its content hash, origin, storage status, subject, layout, and loss status


prov:Activity
The latest journal event for that key


wasGeneratedBy
Association between the key entity and its latest activity


prov:PrimarySource and wasDerivedFrom
An external source recorded by a root ingest


prov:Plan and p-plan:Step
The layout profile and matching rule used for storage


prov:SoftwareAgent and wasAssociatedWith
The software name passed as agent



If a write supplies no ingest source, its target path is used as the source reference. Pass ingest_record when the output was derived from another file or dataset object. See Export data lineage as W3C PROV.

title: Data lineage and provenance
text:
4 Integrity properties
BITS guardrail G3 requires a dataset to retain the provenance information needed to interpret its current content and to identify a trusted manifest state. bitsio stores lineage journals and producer recipes in base datasets and workspaces. A normal discarded-workspace archive retains its journal and producer metadata. freeze() records content and history digests and rejects a dataset with no provenance state to pin.

title: Data lineage and provenance
text:
5 Condense and evert
condense() materializes a computed navigator output as stored data; evert() removes stored data while retaining a recipe that can recompute it. These APIs are part of the tensorbids operation model. The bitsio reference resolver is limited to reconstruction operators, so these operations have limited practical use in a bitsio-only workflow and are not used by the tutorials.

title: Data lineage and provenance
text:
6 Compared with BIDS
BIDS GeneratedBy records pipelines at the derivative-dataset level (Gorgolewski et al. 2016). BITS lineage operates at the stored-key level and records successive events. W3C PROV export projects those entries into entities, activities, sources, plans, and software agents. Applications can use both dataset-level BIDS provenance and key-level BITS lineage.
